content.title: The 2026 Oscars are here: Where to watch, what to know
content.text: March 15, 2026, 6:03 a.m. ET"Sinners" leads this year's Oscar nominees with 16 nominations total, a record-setting number.The broadcast, which airs on ABC and streams on Hulu, will be hosted by Conan O'Brien for the second year in a row.Get the popcorn ready and clear your evening for three to four hours, minimum. The 98th Academy Awards will take place Sunday, March 15, at the Dolby Theatre in Los Angeles.If you're an award season freak like me, your planning for the show started back in January when the nominees were announced. Actually, it probably began shortly after the 2025 statuettes were handed out because a true aficionado tries to see every movie released that generates buzz as Oscar-worthy.Here's a quick guide to everything you need to know about this year's ceremony. Or rather, almost everything. There's still time to flip through a few Oscar history books or squeeze in one more nominated movie like "F1." Yes, the Brad Pitt Formula 1 racing movie got nominated. Buckle up for info below.Where to watch the OscarsThe Academy Awards, aka Hollywood's most glittering gathering, will be shown live at 7 p.m. on ABC and stream live on Hulu. The show also will be streamed on Hulu+ Live TV, YouTubeTV, AT&T TV and FuboTV.If you still have a TV that gets over-the-air signals, you may want to watch the fun the old-school way. Why? Because the Oscars are moving to YouTube in 2029, ending an era of Academy Awards broadcasts on ABC that has lasted since the 1970s.Who is hosting the Oscars?Conan O'Brien, host of the "Conan O'Brien Needs a Friend" podcast and star of HBO Max's travel series "Conan O'Brien Must Go," will preside over the ceremony for the second year running.Here are the Oscar nominees"Sinners" leads the list with a record-breaking 16 nominees, followed by "One Battle After Another" with 13 total nods. The other nominated films are "Bugonia," "F1," "Frankenstein," "Hamnet," "Marty Supreme," "The Secret Agent," "Sentimental Value" and "Train Dreams."Best actor nominees include Timothée Chalamet ("Marty Supreme"), Leonardo DiCaprio ("One Battle After Another"), Ethan Hawke ("Blue Moon"), Michael B. Jordan ("Sinners") Wagner Moura ("The Secret Agent").The best actress contenders are Jessie Buckley ("Hamnet"), Rose Byrne ("If I Had Legs I'd Kick You"), Kate Hudson ("Song Sung Blue"), Renate Reinsve ("Sentimental Value") and Emma Stone ("Bugonia").For a full list of all the categories, go to USAToday.com's coverage.Look for these Oscar presentersAs is traditional, last year's acting winners — Mikey Madison, Adrien Brody, Kieran Culkin and Zoe Saldaña — will help pass out the golden guys to the winners of the four acting categories.Among the other celebrated performers who've been announced as presenters? Javier Bardem, Anne Hathaway, "One Battle After Another" newcomer Chase Infiniti, "Hamnet" star Paul Mescal, "Marty Supreme" star Gwyneth Paltrow, ABC late night host (and past Oscar host) Jimmy Kimmel, best actor nominee for "The Secret Agent" Wagner Moura, father and son duo Bill Pullman and Lewis Pullman and the internet's daddy, Pedro Pascal, to drop a few names.Other things to expectThe broadcast's executive producers have confirmed to the press that there will be a "Bridesmaids" reunion (which Variety earlier reported will feature Kristen Wiig, Maya Rudolph, Melissa McCarthy and current best actress nominee Rose Byrne). They also are teasing some sort of Marvel reunion, if you prefer superheroes over super-funny actresses.Performances are scheduled of two original song nominees, "Golden" from Netflix's "KPop Demon Hunters" and "I Lied to You" from "Sinners." Ejae, Audrey Nuna and Rei Ami are set to sing “Golden,” while "Sinners" star Miles Caton and Raphael Saadiq will be performing “I Lied To You."And a lot of thought is going into the In Memoriam section because of the devastating number of legends lost over the past 12 months. It's a list that includes Robert Redford, Diane Keaton, Gene Hackman, Val Kilmer, Catherine O'Hara and Rob Reiner.What about ABC's coverage of the Oscars red carpet?The network's official red carpet show airs at 6:30 p.m. Sunday, March 15, right before the ceremony kicks off. It will be hosted by Tamron Hall and Jesse Palmer.Pre-coverage of the red carpet (with the ABC team of Linsey Davis, Whit Johnson, Lara Spencer, Chris Connelly and more) will stream on ABC News Live starting at 3:30 p.m. In the Detroit region, WXYZ-TV (Channel 7) will air an hour of it starting at 4:30 p.m.Contact Detroit Free Press pop culture critic Julie Hinds at jhinds@freepress.com.
